newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK rallies to 1,855 forints record high.
newsitem.headline: TVK rallies to 1,855 forints record high.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian chemicals company TVK extended their recent rally on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday to again hit a new high following yet unconfirmed positive news about the company.
TVK shares opened at 1,750 forints, above Tuesday's close of 1,725 and rallied to break a new record of 1,855 forints.
At 1205 GMT TVK stocks stood at 1,835 forints and by that time a huge volume of over 420,000 TVK stocks changed hands.
"The newspaper report stimulated investor interest," said Peter Haas of Postabank Securities. "At the moment nobody knows whether it's true but the price rise was a natural reaction."

Daily economic newspaper Napi Gazdasag reported today that TVK may receive five billion forints from the Hungarian privatisation agency APV Rt on the basis of the country's previous privatisation law. The report said TVK's General Director did not deny the news.
But Haas said a recent roadshow captured foreign investor attention for TVK.
"Since that company presentation abroad foreign investors have increasingly perceived that the share was worth more," Haas said. "A rising number of buying orders are being lodged."
On Monday other market participants attributed TVK's rally to a recent analysis by CS First Boston which maintained an earlier "buy" recommendation.
